## Context / Problem

`tests/unit/test_live_jira_dc_provisioning.py:195`
(`test_a_missing_epic_field_aborts_provisioning`) stubs `_request` so
`/rest/api/2/field` returns a body with `Epic Name` but WITHOUT `Epic Link`, then
calls `harness._assert_project_capabilities("RBTEST")`. The missing field is
permanently absent under the stub, so the readiness poll can only expire — and it
expires against the real PRODUCTION budget.

That budget is `scripts/jira_dc_field_readiness.py:114`,
`FIELD_READY_BUDGET_S = 120.0`, polled every `FIELD_POLL_INTERVAL_S = 1.0`
(line 95). `await_required_fields` (line 226) loops
`request` -> `if monotonic() >= deadline: break` -> `sleep(interval)`, so the unit
test performs ~120 stub reads and sleeps ~120 real seconds to learn something the
stub decided up front. That matches the filed 120.39-121.03s.

The seam is already provided. `_assert_project_capabilities`
(`tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py:580-581`) does NOT rely on the module
constant: it computes `field_budget = _field_ready_timeout()` and passes
`budget=field_budget` explicitly. `_field_ready_timeout()` (line 157) reads the
`JIRA_DC_FIELD_READY_TIMEOUT` environment variable and only falls back to
`FIELD_READY_BUDGET_S` when it is unset. And `await_required_fields` documents
(line 252) that at least one attempt is always made "even with a zero or negative
allowance — the answer must come from an observation, never from arithmetic".

## Approach

Set the readiness budget to zero for this one test through the environment
variable the production code already honours, and assert the resulting poll count.

* `monkeypatch.setenv("JIRA_DC_FIELD_READY_TIMEOUT", "0")` inside the test.
  `monkeypatch` restores the environment at teardown, so no other test and no
  production path sees it; the committed `FIELD_READY_BUDGET_S` stays `120.0`.
  Going through the env var rather than rebinding `FIELD_READY_BUDGET_S` is what
  makes this deterministic: the caller passes `budget=` explicitly, so a constant
  rebind would be silently defeated whenever `JIRA_DC_FIELD_READY_TIMEOUT` is
  already set in the ambient environment, whereas `setenv` overrides it either way.
* With a zero budget the loop is fully DETERMINISTIC rather than merely fast: one
  attempt is made unconditionally, `monotonic() >= deadline` is then true, and the
  loop breaks BEFORE `sleep` is ever called. So the test asserts that the stub saw
  exactly ONE `/rest/api/2/field` read.

That single assertion is the required guard, and it is stronger than a timing
budget: reaching a real sleep is only possible by going round the loop again, which
necessarily produces a second field read and fails the count. It contains no
wall-clock assertion.

`_stub_request` (line 72) already returns its recorded `(method, path, payload)`
list, so the poll count is available without new plumbing.

This is the mechanism the sibling suite already uses —
`tests/unit/test_live_jira_dc_conftest.py:296` sets the same environment variable
for the same reason — so it adds no new pattern to the tree. A fake
`sleep`/`monotonic` pair was rejected: `await_required_fields` accepts them, but
`_assert_project_capabilities` does not forward them, so injecting would mean
changing a production signature to serve a test.

## Scope

* `tests/unit/test_live_jira_dc_provisioning.py` — set the zero budget and assert the
  poll count in `test_a_missing_epic_field_aborts_provisioning`; note why in the
  test docstring.

No production change: `scripts/jira_dc_field_readiness.py` and
`tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py` are read but not modified.

## Testing

* Happy path — the test still raises `AssertionError` naming `Epic Link`, i.e. the
  existing assertion is untouched, and now also pins one field read.
* Failure/edge path — the guard is proven by seeding: temporarily removing the
  `setenv` is confirmed to make the poll-count assertion FAIL (many reads), not
  merely run slowly. Seed reverted, not committed.
* Ambient-environment check — the test is also run with
  `JIRA_DC_FIELD_READY_TIMEOUT=300` already exported, confirming the `setenv`
  overrides an ambient value rather than being defeated by it.
* Isolation check — the neighbouring readiness tests and the rest of the module
  still pass in the same session, confirming `monkeypatch` restored the env.
* Production-default check — `FIELD_READY_BUDGET_S` is still `120.0` in the
  committed tree, read directly from the source.
* Whole-suite regression — the CI pytest command is green.

No wall-clock or timing-budget assertion is added; savings go in ticket comments.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `test_a_missing_epic_field_aborts_provisioning` still raises the same
      `AssertionError` naming `Epic Link` — verified by the unchanged
      `pytest.raises` plus substring assertion still passing.
- [x] The test asserts exactly one `/rest/api/2/field` read, which proves the
      expiry path ran without reaching `sleep` — verified by the new assertion
      passing and by the seeded-budget run failing it.
- [x] The test completes in under 2 seconds where it took ~120s — measured with
      `pytest --durations` and posted as a before/after ticket comment.
- [x] `scripts/jira_dc_field_readiness.py` and
      `tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py` are byte-identical to `origin/main`,
      confirmed by an empty `git diff --stat origin/main -- <those paths>`, so
      production readiness defaults are unchanged.
- [x] The rest of `tests/unit/test_live_jira_dc_provisioning.py` and
      `tests/unit/test_live_jira_dc_conftest.py` pass in one session, showing the
      env override did not leak.
